question: Print a welcome banner for a freshly set up JavaScript project. Build it from a project name and a Node version string held in variables, then log three lines.
Write the smallest useful script. Log a message, then log the type of the value you logged so the output shows both the value and its type.
Print a report about the environment using typeof only: console is available, globalThis is an object, process.argv is an array. Log one line per check.
Write a function parseEnv(text) that turns a KEY=value block into an object. For the text "PORT=3000\nHOST=localhost" return { PORT: "3000", HOST: "localhost" } and log the result.

Write a function parseEnv(text) that ignores blank lines and lines starting with #. For "# a comment
PORT=3000

HOST=localhost" return an object with only PORT and HOST.
Write a function parseEnv(text) that trims whitespace around keys and values and removes surrounding double quotes. For " NAME = \"ana\" " return { NAME: "ana" } and log it.
Write a function getSetting(env, key, fallback) that returns env[key] when the key exists and the fallback otherwise. Log it for a missing key.
Print a small project tree held in an object of file names, then log how many files it contains and each name with its size in bytes.
Write a function printTree(node, indent) that prints a nested object as an indented tree, so a config object shows its shape. Log the result for a small config.
Build a lookup from file extension to runtime (.js to Node.js, .html to the browser, .py to Python) and print which of a list of file names you could run JavaScript on.
Write a function isJsFile(name) that returns true when a file name ends in .js or .mjs. Log the result for index.js, notes.md and tool.mjs.
Write a function countLines(text) that returns how many lines a piece of text has, and log it for a three-line config string.
Write a function stripBlankLines(lines) that removes empty entries from an array of strings and returns the count that survived. Log both the result and the count.
Simulate running a script from the terminal. Build the command string "node app.js" from variables and log it, then log the output the script would print.
Write a function printUsage(script, description, example) that prints a three-line help block. Call it for a script named "seed-db" and log the block.
Build a package scripts lookup (test, lint, start) and write a function runScript(name) that logs the command for a named script or reports it is missing. Call it for "test" and "deploy".
Write a function isSupportedVersion(versionString) that returns true for Node major version 18 or higher. Log the result for "v20.11.1", "v16.20.0" and "v18.0.0".
Write a function checkEnv(required, present) that returns the list of required names that are missing from present. Log the result for required PORT and HOST with only PORT available.
Write a function validateEnv(env) that returns a list of problems: a missing BASE_URL and a PORT that is not a number. Log the problems for a given env object.
Print the contents of a .gitignore file held as an array of lines, and log the line count. Use node_modules, .env and coverage.
Build a project scaffold as an array of file paths and print how many files it creates plus each path numbered. Use package.json, src/index.js, tests/login.test.js and .env.example.
Write a function which(command, installed) that returns the tool name when it is installed and "not found" otherwise. Log the result for node, npm and docker.
Read a list of test cases from an in-memory array and report how many would pass a rule that the name must contain the word "login". Log each result and the totals.
Write a tiny test suite runner that takes named checks, runs each one, prints PASS or FAIL per check and finishes with a one-line summary of passed, failed and total.
Write a function splitArgs(line) that splits a command line into an array of arguments, keeping a double quoted value as one item. For "--env \"local test\"" return ["--env", "local test"].
Write a function slugify(text) that turns a project name into a file name safe form. For "My Test Project" return "my-test-project" and log it.
Predict the output: log Number(""), log Number(" "), log parseInt("42px"), and log the result of [1, 2] + 1. Two of them are not what people expect.
Predict the output: log JSON.stringify of undefined, of a function, of NaN, and of an object with a toJSON method. Show what disappears.
Predict the output: build an array with one item, assign to index 3, then log the length and the array. Show the holes.
Predict the output: log a template-free concatenation of a string and a boolean, log String(false) plus 1, and log the length of the number string "12345".
Write a function compareVersions(a, b) that returns "newer", "older" or "same" for two dotted version strings. Log the result for "v20.1.0" against "v18.3.0" and for two identical versions.
Read a fake log file held in a string and print only the lines that contain "ERROR", plus how many there were. Example log has two ERROR lines and two INFO lines.
Write a function getConfig(userConfig) that merges user settings over a set of defaults, without changing either input. Log the merged object and the original defaults.
Write a function createProject(name) that returns an object describing a new project: name, entry file and an array of test files. Log what it returns for "shop".
Predict the output: log the length of process.argv, log whether the current directory path is a non-empty string, and log that the runtime is Node. All three must be true.
Build an installed-tools table with name and version, and print it in aligned columns using padEnd. Include node, npm and playwright.
Write a function findDuplicates(list) that returns the values that appear more than once. Log the result for a list of package names with three repeats.
Write a function runStep(label, fn) that runs a setup step, catches any error and logs the label with PASS or FAIL. Run three steps where the last one fails.
Predict the output: build an object with a getter-style method, call it twice, and log the returned values along with the counter behind it.
